title: SAT Digital Prep — Complete Study Course
details:
Digital SAT prep course (Reading & Writing + Math) built around skill mastery: rules, patterns, and common traps.

Best results come from combining this course with timed practice questions, full-length practice tests, and an error log (review weekly). Aim to be strong in Module 1 because the test is adaptive.

All content is original and SAT-aligned (not official College Board questions).

modules.moduleDescription: 1. Reading & Writing • Information & Ideas • Main idea, details, inferences, and best-supported conclusions. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Heat maps show shaded blocks are cooler; cooler pavement lasts longer.
Answer: Trees can reduce heat and maintenance costs.
Trap: Don't pick only one benefit.
cards.title: Main Idea: Heat maps show shaded

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Long audio guides distract; museums now use short clips to keep focus on art.
Answer: Shorter audio guides inform without distracting.
Trap: Avoid a title about all museum technology.
cards.title: Main Idea: Long audio guides distract

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Remote teams miss informal questions; written docs reveal assumptions early.
Answer: Documentation prevents small remote-work misunderstandings.
Trap: Don't blame meetings; the point is visibility of assumptions.
cards.title: Main Idea: Remote teams miss informal

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Outdoor irrigation is a major water use; replacing lawns cuts use most.
Answer: Target big water uses to conserve effectively.
Trap: Don't focus on minor habits if text stresses irrigation.
cards.title: Main Idea: Outdoor irrigation is major

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Costs fell for solar panels; adoption rose; market growth lowered costs further.
Answer: Lower prices can accelerate adoption through feedback.
Trap: Don't claim solar is always cheapest.
cards.title: Main Idea: Costs fell solar panels

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Robots save walking time; rushed rollout fails when software doesn't match.
Answer: Automation succeeds when systems are integrated.
Trap: Don't say robots are bad; it's about planning.
cards.title: Main Idea: Robots save walking time

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Chemical tests show similar pots can come from different clay sources.
Answer: Chemistry adds insight beyond surface appearance.
Trap: Don't equate 'similar look' with 'same origin'.
cards.title: Main Idea: Chemical tests show similar

cards.cardDescription:

Trap: Don't generalize to all wildlife.

cards.cardDescription:

cards.cardDescription:

modules.moduleDescription: 2. Reading & Writing • Command of Evidence • Choose evidence that best supports a claim; interpret evidence from tables/graphs. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A city planted trees. Later, average summer street temps dropped by 3°C on shaded blocks.
Answer: Cite the temperature drop as evidence trees reduce heat.
Trap: A statement about 'trees look nice' is not evidence of cooling.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text city planted

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: After switching to reusable mugs, the cafe's spending on disposable cups fell 18%.
Answer: Use the 18% drop to support a cost-savings claim.
Trap: Customer complaints don't support a savings claim.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text After switching

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: In a trial, students who slept after studying recalled 25% more details the next day.
Answer: The 25% increase supports that sleep improves recall.
Trap: 'Students stayed up late' is background, not proof.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text trial students

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A noise study found whale calls overlapped ship frequencies; whales increased call volume near ships.
Answer: Cite overlap + louder calls to support 'ships disrupt communication.'
Trap: 'Scientists use microphones' is context only.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text noise study

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Low-cost sensors varied, but maps consistently highlighted the same pollution hotspot near a highway.
Answer: Cite consistent hotspot mapping to support 'sensors can guide follow-up.'
Trap: Variability alone doesn't prove usefulness.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text Low cost

cards.cardDescription:
Claim: The policy reduced crashes. Mini-text: collisions at three intersections fell from 12 to 5.
Answer: Cite 12→5 as direct evidence of fewer crashes.
Trap: A quote from an opponent isn't evidence.
cards.title: Evidence: Claim policy reduced crashes

cards.cardDescription:
Claim: Electric buses can lower long-term costs. Mini-text: maintenance hours dropped 30% after adoption.
Answer: Cite the 30% maintenance drop.
Trap: Higher upfront cost doesn't prove long-term savings.
cards.title: Evidence: Claim Electric buses can

cards.cardDescription:
Claim: Documentation prevents misunderstandings. Mini-text: teams with shared docs resolved issues faster.
Answer: Cite faster issue resolution in documented teams.
Trap: 'Remote work is hard' is too general.
cards.title: Evidence: Claim Documentation prevents misunderstandings

cards.cardDescription:
Claim: Recycling access affects participation. Mini-text: adding drop-off bins doubled returns.
Answer: Cite 'doubled returns' after bins were added.
Trap: 'Recycling is important' is a value statement.
cards.title: Evidence: Claim Recycling access affects

cards.cardDescription:
Claim: Filters must target micro-particles. Mini-text: the smallest fragments passed through standard mesh.
Answer: Cite 'smallest fragments passed through' as design evidence.
Trap: Chemical absorption is related but not about filters.
cards.title: Evidence: Claim Filters must target evidence

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A translation preserved rhythm but changed wording; reviewers praised the poem's tone.
Answer: Cite praise of tone to support 'effect matters, not literal words.'
Trap: Literal accuracy alone doesn't support tone preservation.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text translation preserved

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A model predicted late-game defense shifts; coaches adjusted and improved fourth-quarter scoring.
Answer: Cite improved scoring after using the model.
Trap: 'Coaches used experience before' is history, not evidence.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text model predicted

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Replacing lawns cut outdoor water use by 40% in one neighborhood.
Answer: Cite the 40% reduction for conservation impact.
Trap: Shorter showers are not evidence for lawn replacement.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text Replacing lawns

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: After adding brief museum clips, visitor dwell time per artwork increased.
Answer: Cite increased dwell time to support 'short clips encourage observation.'
Trap: 'Some visitors ignore labels' is a setup line.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text After adding

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Arctic summer ice thinned; exposed dark water absorbed more sunlight and warmed faster.
Answer: Cite 'dark water absorbed more sunlight' to support a feedback loop claim.
Trap: 'Satellites take images' is background.
cards.title: Evidence: Mini text Arctic summer

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Year 1: 100 bikes/day; Year 2: 160 bikes/day after protected lanes.
Answer: Bike commuting increased after lanes were added (100→160).
Trap: Don't claim lanes caused all increases if other factors aren't mentioned.
cards.title: Data: Mini table Year 1

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Test A (slept): 82 avg; Test B (awake): 65 avg.
Answer: Sleep group scored higher; cite 82 vs 65.
Trap: Don't infer sleep is the only factor.
cards.title: Data: Mini table Test slept

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Cup costs before: $900/month; after reuse: $650/month.
Answer: Costs decreased by $250/month after the change.
Trap: Don't report percent unless asked or computed.
cards.title: Data: Mini table Cup costs

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Readings vary, but hotspot location repeats in 5/5 maps.
Answer: Repeated hotspot location supports hotspot detection reliability.
Trap: Variation doesn't automatically make data useless.
cards.title: Data: Mini table Readings vary

Answer: Electric maintenance is 36 hours lower (120−84).
Trap: Don't claim total cost is lower without fuel/electricity data.
cards.title: Data: Mini table Maintenance hours

cards.cardDescription:

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Choose the line about higher likelihood of dying later.

cards.cardDescription:

cards.cardDescription:

cards.title: Support: Claim Automation depends planning

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Choose the line about hotspots deserving further study.

cards.title: Support: Claim Sensors complement monitoring

cards.cardDescription:

cards.title: Support: Claim Translation involves interpretation

cards.cardDescription:

cards.cardDescription:

cards.title: Support: Claim Strong writing emerges

modules.title: 2. Reading & Writing — Command of Evidence

modules.moduleDescription: 3. Reading & Writing • Craft & Structure • Words in context, tone, purpose, and text structure. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The critic called the sequel 'ambitious,' noting it attempted themes the first film avoided.
Answer: ambitious = daring or aiming high.
Trap: Not 'successful'—it's about scope/aim.
cards.title: Context: Mini text critic called

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The town's 'modest' library fits in one room, but residents praise its helpful staff.
Answer: modest = small or not grand.
Trap: Not 'humble' as a personality trait here.
cards.title: Context: Mini text town's 'modest'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The scientist was 'cautious' in her claims, emphasizing the results were preliminary.
Answer: cautious = careful and not overconfident.
Trap: Not 'fearful'—it's methodological.
cards.title: Context: Mini text scientist 'cautious'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The plan seemed 'inevitable' after every alternative proved more expensive.
Answer: inevitable = unavoidable.
Trap: Not 'immediate'—it's about certainty.
cards.title: Context: Mini text plan seemed

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author 'concedes' that the policy has costs, but argues benefits outweigh them.
Answer: concedes = admits (often reluctantly).
Trap: Not 'celebrates'—it's an acknowledgement.
cards.title: Context: Mini text author 'concedes'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The mayor's proposal 'sparked' debate, with supporters and critics responding quickly.
Answer: sparked = triggered or caused to start.
Trap: Not literally 'caught fire.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text mayor's proposal

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The committee 'deferred' the vote until more data arrived next month.
Answer: deferred = postponed.
Trap: Not 'rejected'—it was delayed.
cards.title: Context: Mini text committee 'deferred'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The discovery 'undermines' the earlier theory by contradicting its key prediction.
Answer: undermines = weakens.
Trap: Not 'destroys' unless stated as total.
cards.title: Context: Mini text discovery 'undermines'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The guide 'elaborates' on the rule by adding two clear examples.
Answer: elaborates = explains in more detail.
Trap: Not 'exaggerates.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text guide 'elaborates'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The writer's tone is 'wry' as she praises the product while hinting at its flaws.
Answer: wry = dryly humorous or subtly ironic.
Trap: Not 'angry'—it's understated.
cards.title: Context: Mini text writer's tone

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The athlete's recovery was 'gradual'; each week she could do a bit more.
Answer: gradual = happening slowly over time.
Trap: Not 'uncertain.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text athlete's recovery

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The historian 'contends' the event was misunderstood, citing new letters as proof.
Answer: contends = argues/claims.
Trap: Not 'admits.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text historian 'contends'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The artist 'refined' the sketch, removing clutter and sharpening the focal point.
Answer: refined = improved by making small changes.
Trap: Not 'made bigger'—it's about polish.
cards.title: Context: Mini text artist 'refined'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The solution is 'viable' because it can be scaled without raising costs much.
Answer: viable = workable/feasible.
Trap: Not 'ideal'—it means possible.
cards.title: Context: Mini text solution 'viable'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The editor 'flagged' unclear sentences, asking the writer to rewrite them.
Answer: flagged = marked for attention.
Trap: Not 'praised.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text editor 'flagged'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The speaker 'qualifies' her statement: 'This is true in most cases, not all.'
Answer: qualifies = limits/softens a claim.
Trap: Not 'certifies.'
cards.title: Context: Mini text speaker 'qualifies'

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Some critics argue...'; the author then answers their objection with data.
Answer: Critics are mentioned to set up a rebuttal.
Trap: Not to agree with the critics.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text 'Some critics

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'For example, two rivers...' follows a general claim about erosion.
Answer: The example illustrates the general claim.
Trap: Not a new, unrelated point.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text 'For example

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author defines 'microplastics' before describing their sources.
Answer: The definition clarifies a key term for readers.
Trap: Not evidence by itself.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text author defines

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A paragraph lists steps (measure, compare, repeat) after describing a method.
Answer: The list explains how to carry out the method.
Trap: Not to criticize the method.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text paragraph lists

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author admits a limitation and then proposes further research.
Answer: The limitation builds credibility before moving forward.
Trap: Not abandoning the argument.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text author admits

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'However,' introduces a sentence that contrasts a common belief.
Answer: It signals a shift to a contrasting idea.
Trap: Not another example.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text 'However '

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author quotes a scientist and then paraphrases the point.
Answer: The quote adds authority and precision.
Trap: Focus on what the quote supports.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text author quotes

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A brief anecdote opens an article about policy effects.
Answer: The anecdote engages readers and introduces the topic.
Trap: Not main evidence unless tied to data.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text brief anecdote

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author repeats a key phrase at the end of each paragraph.
Answer: Repetition emphasizes the central theme.
Trap: Not new information.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text author repeats

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author uses a rhetorical question, then answers it.
Answer: The question frames the issue the author will address.
Trap: Not uncertainty.
cards.title: Purpose: Mini text author uses

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The passage moves from describing a problem to proposing solutions.
Answer: Structure = problem → solution.
Trap: Not cause → effect unless explicit.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text passage moves

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Claim → evidence → counterpoint response across three paragraphs.
Answer: Structure = claim → evidence → rebuttal.
Trap: Don't label evidence as 'new claim.'
cards.title: Structure: Mini text Claim evidence

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author compares two approaches, then judges one as better.
Answer: Structure = comparison → evaluation.
Trap: Not neutral comparison.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text author compares

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The text explains steps of a method and ends with the outcome.
Answer: Structure = process → outcome.
Trap: Not storytelling chronology.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text text explains

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author opens with a surprising fact, then explains why it matters.
Answer: Structure = hook → explanation/implication.
Trap: The hook isn't the thesis alone.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text author opens

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Two experiments are described, then the author connects the findings.
Answer: Structure = two studies → synthesis.
Trap: Don't treat studies as unrelated.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text Two experiments

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author defines a term, gives examples, then draws a conclusion.
Answer: Structure = definition → examples → conclusion.
Trap: Examples support the definition.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text author defines

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The passage summarizes past research, then introduces new work.
Answer: Structure = background → new contribution.
Trap: Background isn't the main claim.
cards.title: Structure: Mini text passage summarizes

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Although impressive, the device still falls short in everyday use.'
Answer: Tone = qualified or mildly critical.
Trap: Not hostile.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'Although impressive

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Fortunately, the new rules simplify the process for everyone.'
Answer: Tone = positive/optimistic.
Trap: Not surprised.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'Fortunately new

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The proposal sounds elegant—until you examine the costs.'
Answer: Tone = skeptical.
Trap: Not confused.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'The proposal

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The results suggest a possibility, though more study is needed.'
Answer: Tone = cautious.
Trap: Not certain.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'The results

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'It's tempting to blame technology, but the evidence points elsewhere.'
Answer: Tone = corrective and analytical.
Trap: Not angry.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'It's tempting

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Remarkably, the tiny sensor performed nearly as well as the lab device.'
Answer: Tone = impressed.
Trap: Not doubtful.
cards.title: Tone: Mini text 'Remarkably tiny

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: In context questions, replace the word with each choice and reread the sentence.
Answer: Choose the option that keeps the meaning and tone.
Trap: A 'fancy' synonym can be wrong in context.
cards.title: Rule: Rule context questions replace

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use nearby clues (contrast, examples, restatements) to infer meaning.
Answer: Notice words like however/although and definition-like phrases.
Trap: Don't rely on the first dictionary meaning.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Use nearby clues

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tone is usually mild on SAT (measured, cautious, skeptical).
Answer: Match intensity: mild language → mild tone word.
Trap: Extreme tones need extreme language.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Tone usually mild

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Purpose/function asks what a sentence does, not what it says.
Answer: Name the job: define, exemplify, rebut, concede, transition, conclude.
Trap: Paraphrasing content isn't function.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Purpose function asks

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Overall structure is the big move between paragraphs.
Answer: Summarize each paragraph in 3–5 words, then connect them.
Trap: Too much detail hides the pattern.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Overall structure big

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A concession often improves credibility before defending a claim.
Answer: Concession = admit a limit, then continue argument.
Trap: Don't treat concession as the thesis.
cards.title: Rule: Rule concession often improves

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Signal words map logic fast (however=contrast, therefore=conclusion).
Answer: Use transitions to predict the sentence's role.
Trap: Ignoring signal words causes wrong tone/purpose.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Signal words map

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Quote/reference questions: ask whether the author endorses or responds.
Answer: The quote may be evidence, a counterpoint, or context.
Trap: Don't assume agreement.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Quote reference questions

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: If two answers seem close, test scope and tone together.
Answer: The correct choice fits both meaning and attitude.
Trap: 'Mostly right' is still wrong.
cards.title: Rule: Rule If two answers

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: For function, check the sentences immediately before and after.
Answer: Function depends on local context, not the whole passage.
Trap: Picking a global role for a local sentence.
cards.title: Rule: Rule function check sentences

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Words in Context (fast SAT check).
Answer: Read sentence. Predict meaning. Plug choices. Recheck tone.
Trap: Don't pick by vibe ; pick by fit.
cards.title: Words in Context

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Tone (fast SAT check).
Answer: Circle evaluative words. Notice qualifiers (may, some). Choose closest attitude.
Trap: One strong word rarely changes whole tone.
cards.title: 3. Reading & Writing — Craft & Structure: Tone

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Purpose/Function (fast SAT check).
Answer: Locate sentence → Ask: why is it here? Link to nearby claim.
Trap: 'What' is not 'why.'
cards.title: Purpose/Function

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Structure (fast SAT check).
Answer: Paragraph summaries. Identify shift. Name pattern (problem-solution, compare-evaluate).
Trap: Mixing up order is a common trap.
cards.title: 3. Reading & Writing — Craft & Structure: Structure

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Quote/Reference (fast SAT check).
Answer: Who is referenced? What point is tied to it? Endorsed, contrasted, or rebutted?
Trap: Treating all quotes as support.
cards.title: Quote/Reference

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Dictionary meaning can mislead.
Answer: The right choice must fit the sentence and surrounding idea.
Trap: Context choices can be generally true but wrong here.
cards.title: Trap: Trap Context choices can

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Content-only answers are wrong type.
Answer: Focus on role (example, counterpoint, definition, transition).
Trap: Purpose questions punish paraphrase.
cards.title: Trap: Trap Purpose questions punish

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Mild language can't support extreme tone.
Answer: Prefer 'qualified/skeptical' over 'furious/overjoyed' unless obvious.
Trap: Tone is rarely extreme on SAT passages.
cards.title: Trap: Trap Tone rarely extreme

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Right pieces in wrong order = wrong.
Answer: Track sequence: background first? claim first? solution last?
Trap: Structure choices often swap order.
cards.title: Trap: Trap Structure choices often

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Don't pick answers saying the author abandons the argument.
Answer: Concession admits something then returns to main claim.
Trap: 'Concession' isn't 'refutation.'

modules.moduleDescription: 4. Reading & Writing • Rhetorical Synthesis • Use notes/bullets to craft the most effective sentence that meets a specific goal. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Pine bark mulch retains moisture; reduces weeds; apply 5–7 cm layer.
Answer: Goal: recommend mulch for low-maintenance gardens.
Trap: Answer: Pine bark mulch helps retain moisture and suppress weeds, making gardens easier to maintain.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Pine bark mulch

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Study found short museum clips increased dwell time; visitors reported less distraction.
Answer: Goal: support using brief audio guides.
Trap: Answer: Brief audio clips can boost engagement by increasing how long visitors examine artworks.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Study found short

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Electric buses cost more upfront; maintenance hours fell 30%; energy prices stable.
Answer: Goal: emphasize long-term savings.
Trap: Answer: Despite higher upfront costs, electric buses can reduce long-term expenses through lower maintenance.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Electric buses cost

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Microplastics enter rivers via tire wear; filters catch large debris; tiny fragments pass through.
Answer: Goal: highlight a limitation of current filtration.
Trap: Answer: Standard filters often miss the smallest microplastic fragments, limiting their effectiveness.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Microplastics enter rivers

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Local turnout low; policies affect transit and zoning; small vote swings decide races.
Answer: Goal: encourage voting in local elections.
Trap: Answer: Because local races are often decided by small margins, voting can have an outsized impact.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Local turnout low

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Coral bleaching weakens corals; survival improves when heat stress is reduced.
Answer: Goal: stress urgency of reducing heat exposure.
Trap: Answer: Reducing heat stress is crucial because bleaching leaves corals weaker and less likely to survive.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Coral bleaching weakens

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Paraphrasing notes improved recall vs verbatim typing; deeper processing suspected.
Answer: Goal: advise a study strategy.
Trap: Answer: Students should paraphrase key ideas because rephrasing promotes deeper processing and better recall.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Paraphrasing notes improved

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Light pollution disrupts star cues for migrating birds; shielded lighting reduces glare.
Answer: Goal: propose a practical city solution.
Trap: Answer: Cities can reduce migration disruption by using shielded lights that limit glare and sky glow.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Light pollution disrupts

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Protected bike lanes added; crashes fell 12→5 at intersections; ridership rose 100→160/day.
Answer: Goal: argue bike lanes improve safety.
Trap: Answer: After protected lanes were added, intersection crashes dropped and ridership increased, suggesting improved safety.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Protected bike lanes

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Goal: explain why adoption accelerated.
Trap: Answer: As panel prices fell, more people adopted solar, creating rapid growth in installations.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Solar panel costs

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Goal: describe libraries as community hubs.
Trap: Answer: Modern libraries serve as community hubs by lending tools, hosting workshops, and providing study space.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Library offers tool

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Goal: support prioritizing effect over literal wording.
Trap: Answer: Reviewers preferred the translation that preserved rhythm and tone, showing effect can matter more than literal wording.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Translation keeps literal

Answer: Goal: emphasize planning for automation.
Trap: Answer: Automation works best when companies plan system integration, not just purchase new machines.
cards.title: Synthesis: Notes Warehouse robots save

Trap: Answer: Low-cost sensors can complement official monitoring by identifying hotspots that merit precise lab follow-up.

cards.title: Synthesis: Notes New trail attracts

modules.moduleDescription: 5. Reading & Writing • Transitions • Select transitions that correctly express logic: contrast, cause/effect, addition, example, sequence, and concession. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The study began in 1998. ____ it expanded to five countries.'
Answer: Later / Over time (signals time progression).
Trap: However implies contrast, not time.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The study

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The device is cheaper. ____ it breaks more often.'
Answer: However / Nevertheless (contrast).
Trap: Therefore implies cause/conclusion.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The device

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy reduced crashes. ____ emergency response improved.'
Answer: In addition / Moreover (adds another benefit).
Trap: In contrast changes direction.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The policy

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Many expected rain. ____ the sky stayed clear.'
Answer: But / Yet (unexpected contrast).
Trap: For example doesn't fit.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'Many expected

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The first trial failed; ____ researchers revised the design.'
Answer: therefore / as a result (cause → response).
Trap: Similarly isn't causal.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The first

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Some residents favor the plan; ____ others worry about taxes.'
Answer: while / whereas (two sides).
Trap: Thus is not comparison.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'Some residents

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The museum cut audio length. ____ visitors spent longer viewing art.'
Answer: As a result (cause → effect if relationship stated).
Trap: Meanwhile is only timing.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The museum

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The paper reports averages. ____ it includes confidence intervals.'
Answer: Additionally (adds detail).
Trap: Consequently suggests an outcome.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The paper

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The author defines the term. ____ she provides two examples.'
Answer: Then / Next (sequence).
Trap: Therefore implies conclusion.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The author

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The method is simple. ____ it requires careful calibration.'
Answer: Even so / However (qualification).
Trap: Likewise doesn't qualify.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The method

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The town built bike lanes; ____ ridership rose.'
Answer: and / afterward / subsequently (timing or addition).
Trap: Because implies ridership caused lanes.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The town

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The sample was small; ____ the trend is worth studying.'
Answer: nonetheless (concession).
Trap: therefore is too strong.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The sample

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The artist revised the sketch; ____ the final image feels clearer.'
Answer: as a result (revision → clarity).
Trap: on the other hand shifts comparison.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The artist

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team reduced emissions 12%. ____ they optimized delivery routes.'
Answer: For instance (introduces an example of how).
Trap: Consequently doesn't introduce an example.
cards.title: Transition: Mini text 'The team

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The results were promising ____ the study was small.'
Answer: ; / . (new sentence) or , but (needs conjunction).
Trap: Comma splice with comma alone.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The results

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The plan is viable ____ it will require funding.'
Answer: , but (contrast) or ; however, (new clause).
Trap: , however (without semicolon/period) is wrong.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The plan

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The device is durable ____ it survived the stress test.'
Answer: because (reason) or ; it survived... (two sentences).
Trap: A semicolon can't replace 'because' if you need causation.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The device

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The author concedes a limitation ____ she continues her argument.'
Answer: , and (sequence) or ; then (new sentence).
Trap: , therefore (wrong logic).
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The author

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Researchers collected samples ____ they analyzed them later.'
Answer: and (same sentence) or . They analyzed... (split).
Trap: Comma alone is a splice.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'Researchers collected

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy is popular ____ its costs are unclear.'
Answer: though / although (concession).
Trap: because flips meaning.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The policy

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The guide explains the rule ____ it adds two examples.'
Answer: and (addition) or . It adds... (split).
Trap: ; and is often redundant.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The guide

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The town planted trees ____ the streets became cooler.'
Answer: and / so (result) depending on meaning.
Trap: because would reverse cause/effect.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The town

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The survey had a low response rate ____ the results may be biased.'
Answer: so / therefore (conclusion) or ; thus, (two clauses).
Trap: , therefore with comma only is wrong.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The survey

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'She revised the draft ____ deleting off-topic paragraphs.'
Answer: by (method) or , deleting... (appositive-style).
Trap: because changes relationship.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'She revised

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The program was successful. It was successful because costs fell.'
Answer: Combine: The program was successful because costs fell.
Trap: Don't repeat the same claim twice.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The program

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Many residents disagree. Residents have different opinions.'
Answer: Combine: Residents hold differing opinions.
Trap: Avoid repeating the same idea in new words.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'Many residents

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The device is lightweight. It weighs only 1.2 pounds.'
Answer: Combine: The lightweight device weighs only 1.2 pounds.
Trap: Don't drop the number.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The device

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The plan is feasible. It can be implemented without raising costs.'
Answer: Combine: The plan is feasible because it can be implemented without raising costs.
Trap: Don't add new reasons.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The plan

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The study was small. However, the results were promising.'
Answer: Combine: Although the study was small, the results were promising.
Trap: Keep the contrast.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The study

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'He revised the sketch. He refined the lines to improve clarity.'
Answer: Combine: He refined the sketch's lines to improve clarity.
Trap: Don't keep both verbs if one is redundant.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'He revised

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The town built lanes. This led to more biking.'
Answer: Combine: After the town built lanes, biking increased.
Trap: Avoid vague 'this' without a clear referent.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The town

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy reduced crashes. It reduced crashes at intersections.'
Answer: Combine: The policy reduced intersection crashes.
Trap: Remove the repeated phrase.
cards.title: Concise: Mini text 'The policy

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'When the team met with the managers, they were frustrated.'
Answer: Clarify who: The managers were frustrated (or the team...).
Trap: 'They' is ambiguous.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'When team

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'After reviewing the report, the decision was obvious.'
Answer: Fix modifier: After reviewing the report, the committee found the decision obvious.
Trap: Dangling modifier (who reviewed?).
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'After reviewing

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The scientist told the assistant that she should publish.'
Answer: Clarify: The scientist told the assistant to publish.
Trap: 'She' could refer to either person.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'The scientist

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Running quickly, the finish line appeared.'
Answer: Fix: Running quickly, the runner saw the finish line.
Trap: Finish line can't run.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'Running quickly

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The company told customers about the update, which was confusing.'
Answer: Specify: The update was confusing (or the message was confusing).
Trap: 'Which' can attach to the wrong noun.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'The company

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The book on the table near the window fell.'
Answer: Reduce clutter: The book near the window fell off the table.
Trap: Misplaced phrases can change meaning.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'The book

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'She gave her sister's friend the gift.'
Answer: Clarify: She gave the gift to her sister's friend.
Trap: Possessives can tangle meaning.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'She gave

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The professor discussed the student with the dean.'
Answer: Clarify: The professor and the dean discussed the student.
Trap: 'With' creates ambiguity.
cards.title: Clarity: Mini text 'The professor

Answer: 'After reading the report, the committee...'

cards.title: Sentence boundary

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Paragraph explains solar costs. Added sentence: 'Many people enjoy sunny weather.'
Answer: Delete it—it's off-topic and doesn't support the point.
Trap: Related word ('sunny') doesn't make it relevant.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Paragraph explains solar costs

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Passage argues for bike lanes. Added sentence describes the inventor of the bicycle.
Answer: Remove—historical trivia doesn't advance the argument.
Trap: Interesting ≠ relevant.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Passage argues bike lanes Added sentence

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author defines microplastics. Added sentence lists restaurant plastics bans.
Answer: Keep only if it supports the definition's purpose; otherwise cut.
Trap: Don't add new subtopics.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text author defines microplastics Added sentence lists

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A study compares sleep vs awake recall. Added sentence: 'Sleep is relaxing for many.'
Answer: Delete—it's opinion, not evidence.
Trap: Avoid value statements in informational passages.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text study compares sleep vs awake recall Added senten

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The passage describes coral bleaching. Added line explains what 'ocean' means.
Answer: Delete—definition is unnecessary and distracts.
Trap: Over-explaining common words.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text passage describes

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: A paragraph lists steps of a method. Added line: 'Scientists often wear lab coats.'
Answer: Remove—doesn't clarify steps or results.
Trap: Visual detail doesn't help reasoning.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text paragraph lists steps method

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Author recommends recycling bins. Added line: 'Recycling logos are common.'
Answer: Delete—doesn't support recommendation or data.
Trap: Same topic ≠ same purpose.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Author recommends recycling bins Added line

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Passage compares two translations. Added line about the translator's birthplace.
Answer: Remove—biography doesn't affect the comparison.
Trap: Don't mistake context for support.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Passage compares two translations Added line abou

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Article discusses light pollution. Added line explains how eyes see light.
Answer: Keep only if the passage needs that mechanism; otherwise cut.
Trap: Unused mechanism is clutter.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Article discusses light pollution Added line expl

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: Counterargument paragraph adds a sentence repeating the main claim.
Answer: Delete repetition; keep the rebuttal evidence.
Trap: Repeating claims wastes space.
cards.title: Relevance: Mini text Counterargument paragraph

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The sensor was good.' Context: it matched lab readings closely.
Answer: Replace with 'accurate' or 'consistent with lab readings.'
Trap: 'Good' is vague; SAT prefers precise.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The sensor good '

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The plan had an effect.' Context: it reduced crashes by 50%.
Answer: Specify: 'reduced crashes by 50%.'
Trap: Avoid empty nouns like 'effect' without detail.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The plan had effect ' Context

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Use the exact claim: 'returns doubled after bins were added.'
Trap: Don't generalize beyond the data.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'Many people recycle ' Context bins doubled retur

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy was bad for some.' Context: taxes rose slightly.
Answer: Replace with 'raised taxes slightly' (specific).
Trap: 'Bad' is opinion; use measured language.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The policy bad some ' Context taxes rose slightl

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The device is smaller.' Context: it is 20% lighter.
Answer: Use measurable terms: '20% lighter' or 'more compact.'
Trap: Don't invent measurements not given.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The device

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The project is important.' Context: it prevents delays and saves money.
Answer: Replace with benefits: 'reduces delays and saves money.'
Trap: Importance claims are vague.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The project important '

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The method changed.' Context: researchers adjusted calibration settings.
Answer: Replace with 'researchers recalibrated the device.'
Trap: 'Changed' hides what happened.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The method changed ' Context researchers

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The results were surprising.' Context: tiny sensor matched lab device.
Answer: Replace with 'performed nearly as well as the lab device.'
Trap: Don't overstate surprise.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The results surprising ' Context tiny sensor mat

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The author talks about parks.' Context: debate about taxes for park funding.
Answer: Specify: 'debates funding parks and taxes.'
Trap: Topic label ≠ main point.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The author talks about parks ' Context debate ab

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Improved efficiency.' Context: fewer steps and fewer forms.
Answer: Specify: 'reduced steps and paperwork.'
Trap: Efficiency without mechanism is vague.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'Improved efficiency

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The trend went up.' Context: 100→160/day.
Answer: State the change: 'increased from 100 to 160 per day.'
Trap: 'Went up a lot' is imprecise.
cards.title: Precision: Mini text 'The trend went up

cards.cardDescription:

Answer: Use 'critical' or 'skeptical,' not 'against.'

cards.title: Concision: Mini text 'The committee postponed vote until later ' Answe

cards.title: Concision: Mini text 'A total

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence adds another benefit but begins 'however

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence restates

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence contrasts two options

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence provides reason but begins 'in

cards.cardDescription:

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence introduces example but begins 'therefore

cards.cardDescription:

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text Sentence summarizes but begins 'for example ' Ans

cards.title: Coherence: Mini text sentence shifts

cards.title: Rule: Rule Prefer active specific verbs empty verbs has Answer Strong

cards.title: Rule: Rule Remove redundancy repeated

cards.title: Rule: Rule Choose transitions match logic contrast

cards.title: Rule: Rule Maintain consistent formal style academic passages Answer

cards.title: Rule: Rule When revising keep sentence adds new information not repeti

modules.moduleDescription: 7. Reading & Writing • Punctuation & Sentence Boundaries • Commas, semicolons, colons, dashes; avoid run-ons and fragments. (Compact set: 90 high-impact flashcards.)

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The results were promising, the sample was small.'
Answer: Fix comma splice: use . ; or add a conjunction (but/and).
Trap: A comma alone can't join two sentences.
cards.title: Comma: Mini text 'The results promising sample

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'After reviewing the report, the team decided to delay.'
Answer: Correct: introductory phrase + comma.
Trap: Don't drop comma if opening phrase is long.
cards.title: Comma: Mini text 'After reviewing report team decided delay

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The museum, which opened in 1920, hosts free lectures.'
Answer: Correct: nonessential clause set off by commas.
Trap: Essential clauses shouldn't be bracketed by commas.
cards.title: Comma: Mini text 'The museum which opened 1920 hosts free lectures

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Students who sleep after studying, perform better.'
Answer: Remove comma: essential clause (who sleep...) shouldn't be separated.
Trap: Comma changes meaning and breaks grammar.
cards.title: Comma: Mini text 'Students who sleep after studying perform better ' A

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'In 2024 the city added bike lanes.'
Answer: Optional comma after short intro; more important is clarity.
Trap: Don't insert commas randomly.
cards.title: Comma: Mini text 'In 2024

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy cut crashes; it also increased ridership.'
Answer: Correct: semicolon joins two related independent clauses.
Trap: Both sides must be complete sentences.
cards.title: Semicolon: Mini text 'The policy cut crashes

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team studied rainfall; because drought was severe.'
Answer: Wrong: second half is a fragment; use comma + because or rewrite.
Trap: Semicolon can't join a fragment.
cards.title: Semicolon: Mini text 'The team studied rainfall because drought

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The device is cheaper; however, it breaks more often.'
Answer: Correct punctuation for 'however' as a transition.
Trap: ', however' between sentences is a comma splice.
cards.title: Semicolon: Mini text 'The device cheaper however breaks more often '

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The study had one clear result: sleep improved recall.'
Answer: Correct: colon introduces explanation after a complete clause.
Trap: Don't use a colon after a fragment.
cards.title: Colon: Mini text 'The study had one clear result sleep improved recall

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team improved three things: speed, accuracy, and cost.'
Answer: Correct: colon introduces a list.
Trap: Don't place a colon right after a verb if the left side isn't complete.
cards.title: Colon: Mini text 'The team

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Because the sample was small: the conclusion is tentative.'
Answer: Wrong: left side is not a complete sentence; remove colon.
Trap: Colons need a full sentence before them.
cards.title: Colon: Mini text 'Because sample small conclusion

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The solution—though expensive—worked immediately.'
Answer: Correct: paired dashes set off an aside.
Trap: Use two dashes (or none), not one.
cards.title: Dash: Mini text 'The solution though expensive worked immediately

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The plan was simple— it required training.'
Answer: Usually wrong spacing/logic; better: ';' or 'but' depending on meaning.
Trap: Dashes don't fix sentence boundaries.
cards.title: Dash: Mini text 'The plan simple required training ' Answer Usually

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The report lists causes—costs, delays, and shortages.'
Answer: Dash can introduce an explanation/list (like a colon).
Trap: Keep style consistent; avoid random dashes.
cards.title: Dash: Mini text 'The report lists causes costs delays shortages ' Answ

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy (first proposed in 2019) passed easily.'
Answer: Correct: parentheses set off extra information like commas.
Trap: Don't break the sentence with mismatched punctuation.
cards.title: Parentheses: Mini text 'The policy

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy (first proposed in 2019 passed easily.'
Answer: Fix: close the parenthesis, or rewrite without it.
Trap: Unbalanced punctuation is an instant error.
cards.title: Parentheses: Mini text 'The policy first proposed

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The students' scores increased after practice.'
Answer: Correct: plural possession (scores of multiple students).
Trap: Don't use apostrophes for simple plurals.
cards.title: Apostrophe: Mini text 'The students' scores increased after practice

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Its effects were clear; it's a strong result.'
Answer: its=possessive, it's=it is.
Trap: Mixing them is a common SAT trap.
cards.title: Apostrophe: Mini text 'Its effects clear it's strong result ' Answer

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The company's policy changed. The companies policy changed.'
Answer: Add apostrophe in company's (one company).
Trap: Plural companies ≠ singular possessive.
cards.title: Apostrophe: Mini text 'The company's policy changed companies policy c

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: The author calls the plan "efficient" but then lists hidden costs.
Answer: Quotes may signal skepticism/irony about the word.
Trap: Don't read quoted words as full endorsement.
cards.title: Quote: Mini text author calls

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The report states, "results are preliminary," and urges caution.'
Answer: Quote provides evidence/authority for caution.
Trap: Don't ignore what the quote supports.
cards.title: Quote: Mini text 'The report states results

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The study was small; therefore the claim is limited.'
Answer: Better: 'The study was small; therefore, the claim is limited.'
Trap: Transition adverbs need comma after them.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The study small therefore claim limited

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The study was small, therefore the claim is limited.'
Answer: Fix: '. Therefore,' or '; therefore,' or 'so'.
Trap: Comma + therefore is often wrong.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The study small therefore claim limited ' Answer

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The plan is viable it will require funding.'
Answer: Add boundary: . ; or , but (depending on logic).
Trap: Run-on sentences are common.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The plan viable will require funding ' Answer Add

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Although the data are limited the trend is clear.'
Answer: Add comma after dependent clause: 'limited, the trend...'
Trap: Missing comma can confuse structure.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'Although data

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'After reading the article, the conclusion was obvious.'
Answer: Fix dangling modifier: name the doer (the committee found...).
Trap: Conclusions can't read.
cards.title: Modifier: Mini text 'After reading article conclusion

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Walking to the station, the rain soaked my bag.'
Answer: Fix: 'While I walked..., the rain soaked my bag.'
Trap: Put the real subject after the modifier.
cards.title: Modifier: Mini text 'Walking station rain soaked my bag

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The program aims to reduce costs, improving quality, and it will expand access.'
Answer: Make parallel: reduce costs, improve quality, and expand access.
Trap: Mixed forms break parallelism.
cards.title: Parallel: Mini text 'The program aims reduce costs improving quality w

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'She values accuracy, clarity, and to be concise.'
Answer: Fix: accuracy, clarity, and concision (or being concise).
Trap: Keep list items in same form.
cards.title: Parallel: Mini text 'She values accuracy clarity concise ' Answer Fix

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'Marie Curie a pioneering scientist won two Nobel Prizes.'
Answer: Add commas: 'Marie Curie, a pioneering scientist, won...'
Trap: Appositives need commas if nonessential.
cards.title: Appositive: Mini text 'Marie Curie

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'My friend, Alex enjoys hiking.'
Answer: Remove comma if Alex is essential; or add second comma if nonessential.
Trap: One comma around an appositive is often wrong.
cards.title: Appositive: Mini text 'My friend Alex enjoys

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The project reduced delays improved accuracy and saved money.'
Answer: Add commas and conjunction: 'reduced delays, improved accuracy, and saved money.'
Trap: Missing separators create confusion.
cards.title: List: Mini text 'The project reduced delays improved accuracy

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The policy affects zoning, transit, and schools.'
Answer: Correct: clear list with commas.
Trap: Don't insert comma before 'and' unless needed.
cards.title: List: Mini text 'The policy affects zoning transit schools ' Answer

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The buses that run on electricity, reduce maintenance costs.'
Answer: Remove comma: 'that' clause is essential.
Trap: Comma after 'that' is usually wrong.
cards.title: Nonessential: Mini text 'The buses run electricity reduce maintenance

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The buses, which run on electricity, reduce maintenance costs.'
Answer: Correct: 'which' clause is nonessential info.
Trap: Choose which/that based on meaning.
cards.title: Nonessential: Mini text 'The buses

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The sensor was accurate; matching lab readings closely.'
Answer: Wrong: second half is a fragment; rewrite or use comma + phrase.
Trap: Semicolon requires a full clause.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The sensor accurate matching

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team recalibrated the sensor; and accuracy improved.'
Answer: Remove 'and' or use comma+and without semicolon.
Trap: Don't stack joiners.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The team recalibrated sensor accuracy improved

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team recalibrated the sensor, and accuracy improved.'
Answer: Correct: comma+and joins two independent clauses.
Trap: Ensure both sides are complete.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The team recalibrated sensor accuracy improved '

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team recalibrated the sensor, accuracy improved.'
Answer: Fix comma splice: add conjunction or split.
Trap: Comma alone is not enough.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The team recalibrated sensor accuracy improv dash

cards.cardDescription:
Mini-text: 'The team recalibrated the sensor. Accuracy improved.'
Answer: Correct: two short sentences can be clearest.
Trap: Don't force complex punctuation.
cards.title: Boundary: Mini text 'The team

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Two complete sentences cannot be joined with a comma alone.
Answer: Use . ; or , + conjunction.
Trap: Comma splice = automatic error.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Two complete sentences cannot joined

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A semicolon joins two related independent clauses.
Answer: Both sides must be complete sentences.
Trap: Semicolon + fragment is wrong.
cards.title: Rule: Rule semicolon joins two related independent clauses Answer

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: A colon introduces a list or explanation AFTER a complete sentence.
Answer: If you can't put a period before it, don't use a colon.
Trap: Colon after a fragment is wrong.
cards.title: Rule: Rule colon introduces list explanation AFTER complete sentence A

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use commas to set off nonessential information; do not set off essential clauses.
Answer: Essential=needed to identify; Nonessential=extra detail.
Trap: Wrong commas change meaning.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Use commas set off nonessential information do not set off

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: 'However/therefore' as transitions need strong punctuation.
Answer: ; however,  |  . Therefore,  |  not ', however' between sentences.
Trap: Comma + transition often creates a splice.
cards.title: Rule: Rule 'However therefore' transitions

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Introductory dependent clauses often need a comma.
Answer: 'Although X, Y' is a reliable pattern.
Trap: Missing comma can cause misreading.
cards.title: Rule: Rule Introductory dependent clauses often need

cards.cardDescription:
Rule: Use apostrophes for possession, not for plurals.

Answer: Difference of squares → (x-3)(x+3)=0 → x=±3.

Answer: AC method: 2·3=6; split 7→6+1 → (2x+1)(x+3)=0.

Answer: x=-b/(2a)=6/2=3; y=9-18+5=-4 → (3,-4).
